1-3.title: Piecewise-Defined Functions
1-3.status: PLC draft, Tue Oct 6 2026 (packet not yet re-cut)

objectives.learning: I can graph a piecewise-defined function and write its rule from a graph.
objectives.language: I can explain, in writing, which rule applies on each part of the domain, using the words piece, interval, open circle and closed circle.
objectives.essentialQuestion: How do you model a situation where different rules apply to different parts of the domain?

quizFocus.what: Which rule defines the function in the graph? Two linear pieces; the four choices differ by the slope of the right piece (-3x+9 vs x-3) and by the endpoint inequalities (< vs <=).
quizFocus.answer: B: x-1 if -3 <= x < 1; -3x+9 if 2 <= x <= 4 (read from the graph; verify against the TE key)
needs: slope of each piece from two points (IXL W67)
open circle = strict inequality, closed dot = inclusive (no IXL skill; whiteboard drill)

dok3.task: Yama's monthly earnings vs. hours worked, plotted as points (10,200), (20,400), ... (100,2900) joined by segments from (0,0). Write the piecewise function for earnings as a function of hours.

modelDiscuss.situation: A music teacher buys guitar strings. Store A sells a single pack for $6; Store B sells a bundle of 4 packs for $20.
studentPrompts: A. Make graphs that show the income each store receives if the teacher needs 1-20 packs.
B. Describe the shape of each store's graph. Why are the graphs different?
C. Communicate Precisely: for what numbers of strings is it cheaper to buy from Store B? Explain how you know. (4, 7, 8, 11, 12, 14-20)

teQuestions.q: How do stores A and B compare?
teQuestions.a: Store A sells strings individually; Store B sells them in packages of 4.

teQuestions.q: How do the stores' graphs represent the cost of the guitar strings?
teQuestions.a: Store A rises steadily, $6 more per string. Store B is constant at $20 for 1-4 strings, then jumps $20 and is constant again.

teQuestions.q: How can you represent the stores' prices as equations?
teQuestions.a: Store A: y = 6x. Store B: y = 20 for 0 < x <= 4, 40 for 4 < x <= 8, 60 for 8 < x <= 12, 80 for 12 < x <= 16, 100 for 16 < x <= 20.

teQuestions.q: What is different about the shapes of the two graphs?
teQuestions.a: Graph A is linear; graph B is a set of horizontal segments (a step function).

teQuestions.q: Why do you use dots rather than line segments to graph these two functions?
teQuestions.a: Dots show whole numbers of strings only; you cannot buy a fraction of a string.

modelDiscuss.caution: The opener is a step-function situation (Example 5 content, cut). It still works as the hook; only the early-finishers equations question leads toward Example 3.

1-2.title: Transformations of Functions
1-2.status: Draft, Tue Oct 6 2026, from the Sep 27 packet plan (Examples 1-5, focus Ex 5, Try It 5 graded, Ex 6 dropped); PLC has not re-cut this packet yet

objectives.learning: I can tell which transformations (left/right, up/down, stretch, reflection) turn a parent graph into a new graph.
objectives.language: I can describe a transformation in writing using the words left, right, up, down, stretch, compress and reflect.
objectives.essentialQuestion: How do the values a, b, h and k in a·f(b(x − h)) + k move or reshape the graph of f?

quizFocus.source: aga_24_a2_na_0102_lq.pdf; the only 1-2 item carried into the Topic 1 assessment (end of October)
quizFocus.what: Select all the transformations of f(x) = x^2 that produce the graph of g (downward parabola, vertex (-1, -2)). Choices: A 1 left, B 1 right, C 2 down, D horizontal stretch by 2, E vertical stretch by 2, F reflection across the x-axis.
quizFocus.answer: A, C, D, F (TE key): 1 left, 2 down, horizontal stretch by 2, reflect across the x-axis. g(x) = -(1/2 (x+1))^2 - 2.
needs: read the vertex and use the sign rule: (x + 1) is 1 LEFT, -2 is 2 down (Example 1, IXL F6J)
opens down = reflection across the x-axis (Example 2, IXL PHV)
wider than x^2 = horizontal stretch, not vertical stretch; check a point one unit from the vertex (Example 3, IXL NNY)
put it together from the graph with no equation given (Example 5, IXL KT8 / R7X)

dok3.label: Practice & Problem Solving 17, Error Analysis (Example 5 DOK 3; item 37 is the SAT/ACT alternative)
dok3.task: Monisha compares f(x) = |x| and g(x) = |2x - 4|. She says g is f translated 4 right and compressed horizontally by 2. What is her error?
dok3.key: |2x - 4| = 2|x - 2|, so g is f translated 2 right and stretched vertically by 2 (or, read as f(2(x - 2)), compressed horizontally by 1/2 and shifted 2 right).
dok3.why: Students must factor inside the absolute value before reading the transformations; the same inside-vs-outside reasoning as quiz item 1's choice D vs E.

modelDiscuss.source: 2024 TE, Step 1 Explore (this lesson's opener is Explore & Reason, powered by Desmos)
modelDiscuss.situation: The graph of f(x) = |x| is shown. Students graph g(x) = |x + c| for several values of c from -5 to 5.
studentPrompts: A. Graph g(x) = |x + c| several times with different values of c (any value from -5 to 5).
B. Look for Relationships: predict what happens to the graph if c is greater than 100. What if c is between 0 and 1/2? (Very large shift left; very small shift left.)

teQuestions.q: What does the graph tell you about the range of f(x) = |x|?
teQuestions.a: The range is greater than or equal to zero.

teQuestions.q: What can you predict about the range of g(x) = |x + c| for different values of c?
teQuestions.a: Whatever c is, the range is still greater than or equal to zero.

teQuestions.q: How can you find points to graph for each function?
teQuestions.a: Make a table of values for x from -5 to 5 and compute y.

teQuestions.q: What do you notice about the vertex of each function?
teQuestions.a: The vertices all lie on the x-axis.

teQuestions.q: How does the graph change if the coefficient of f(x + c) is negative? Graph -f(x + c) for three of your functions.
teQuestions.a: The graphs of -f(x + c) are reflections of f(x + c) across the x-axis.

teQuestions.q: If f(x) has a horizontal shift, what part of the function has been changed?
teQuestions.a: x stands for the domain, so the operation is applied to x inside the parentheses.

teQuestions.q: If f(x) has a vertical shift, what part of the function has been changed?
teQuestions.a: f(x) stands for the range, so the operation is applied to f(x).

teQuestions.q: What happens to the graph if c is a negative number?
teQuestions.a: The graph shifts to the right when c is negative.

modelDiscuss.caution: The After questions are the moment to introduce a·f(b(x - h)) + k. The Mon/Tue whiteboard table activity (a2_1-2_plan_oct5-7) already does part A on paper; the TE's 'table of values' answer matches it.
